subject: Role expectations, short-term checkpoints, and next steps
messages:
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai; evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial alignment — short-term concerns and proposed checkpoints

Marcus / Evelyn --

Following our 1:1 this morning, I wanted to put the items we discussed into an explicit set of expectations and checkpoints for the next 30 days so we have a shared record. This is not a formal PIP today; it is a documented, time-bound coaching plan to address recurring execution and collaboration gaps. I’ll host weekly 30-minute check-ins to keep us aligned.

Primary concerns I observed (examples):
- Missed delivery on two Q3 feature tasks where the rollout schedule slipped without escalation.
- Repeated partial handoffs to Product/QA; unclear ownership on follow-ups.
- Several PRs shipped with high-risk comments that required rework and delayed integrations.

Clear expectations for the next 30 days (measurable):
1) On-time delivery: Meet sprint commitments for the next two sprints. If a task is sliding, notify me and Product within 48 hours with a mitigation plan.
2) Ownership of handoffs: For each story, add a short Handoff Checklist in the PR description (owners, test steps, rollout notes).
3) Quality bar: Reduce rework rate by 50% on code review comments flagged as "functional" or "blocking."

Success metrics / checkpoints:
- Weekly sync on Fri: quick run-through of open items (15 mins) + 30-min deep check weekly (my calendar).
- Milestones recorded in 30_day_checkpoints.xlsx (attached).

I’ve attached a brief observation log and a template we can use to capture progress. Evelyn — tagging you for visibility so we align on documentation and any required HR steps.

Next steps: Marcus, can you confirm availability for a weekly Friday 10:00 AM check-in and reply with any questions or constraints by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: behavioral_observations-20260914.pdf (summary), 30_day_checkpoints.xlsx (workbook)

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial alignment — short-term concerns and proposed checkpoints

Thanks for the write-up, Karthik — and for taking time to make the expectations concrete. I appreciate the clarity. I can do Friday 10:00 AM for the weekly check-in.

Quick context from my side: the two late rollouts were related to unexpected infra flakiness and an incomplete test harness for the feature flags; I should have escalated earlier. I’ll add the handoff checklist to every PR this week and will populate the checkpoints workbook with the stories I own.

One ask: can you share examples of PR descriptions you consider "good" for handoffs? It would be helpful to have a template I can follow in the next 24 hours.

—Marcus

Redwood Inference

Thanks for the loop, Karthik. I reviewed the observations and the proposed checkpoints. A few HR notes to keep the process clean: 

- Documented coaching is best practice. Label the folder "Informal Improvement Plan" in the People Drive.
- Keep notes objective: dates, outcomes, and direct impact on project timelines. Avoid subjective language.
- Provide Marcus with the opportunity to respond in writing; his reply should be saved in the folder.
- If the 30-day checkpoints do not show meaningful progress, we will discuss next steps (which may include a formal PIP).

I attached an "HR improvement template" you can use to summarize weekly check-ins and outcomes (hr_improvement_template.docx). You can use that to track the 30-day plan and to escalate formally if needed.

I recommend we capture the first weekly check-in as a short note in the workbook (who attended, topics, agreements).

Evelyn Hart
People Business Partner
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hr_improvement_template.docx

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai; evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 21:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial alignment — short-term concerns and proposed checkpoints (30-day summary)

Marcus / Evelyn —

We completed the 30-day window today and I wanted to capture the summary:

What improved:
- Marcus consistently updated PRs with a handoff checklist (all tracked in the workbook).
- Two smaller stories landed on time; larger feature remains in progress but with a clear mitigation plan.
- Code review rework rate decreased (~40% improvement on functional comments).

Open areas / next steps:
- Still seeing intermittent delays when infra issues arise; Marcus committed to looping infra earlier and to adding an escalation bullet in sprint planning.
- We agreed one additional 30-day extension of informal coaching to verify sustainable improvement. New checkpoint end date: 2026-11-04.

Evelyn, per our policy please confirm if we are good to keep this as an "Informal Improvement Plan" for now and if the documentation is sufficient.

Marcus — thanks for your engagement here. Please add any comments or corrections to the workbook by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Karthik

Attachments: 30_day_checkpoints.xlsx (updated)
